summary: Resize the current Chrome window or page viewport from built-in presets or your own saved sizes.
singlePurpose: Resize the current Chrome browser window or active page viewport to a user-selected saved width and height.

permissions.name: storage
permissions.justification: Stores the user's custom window-size presets and preferred preset order locally on their device.

permissions.name: activeTab
permissions.justification: Temporarily accesses the current tab after the user opens the extension so viewport-targeted presets can measure the page area.

permissions.name: scripting
permissions.justification: Runs a small local measurement function in the active tab to read its viewport width and height; it does not read or modify page content.

remoteCode.justification: The extension does not use remote code. All executable JavaScript and CSS is included in the submitted package.

store.description:
OSBE Window Resizer gives you repeatable browser and viewport sizes without opening developer tools or typing dimensions every time.

Choose a built-in mobile, tablet, laptop, or desktop preset and the current Chrome window resizes immediately. Each preset can target the complete window or the active page viewport. Add named custom presets using the current target dimensions as a starting point, then edit, reorder, or delete them from the same compact popup.

WHAT IT INCLUDES

- Six built-in device window sizes
- Window or viewport target per preset
- One-click resizing from the toolbar
- Custom presets prefilled from the selected target
- Simple edit, delete, reorder, and reset controls
- Local-only storage
- No account, analytics, ads, tracking, or remote code

Window dimensions include the complete Chrome frame. Viewport dimensions apply to the page area and automatically compensate for browser chrome.

OSBE extensions are open source and focused on one job.

screenshots.title: Resize a Chrome window or viewport with one click.
screenshots.description: The popup shows current window and viewport sizes, built-in presets, and controls for creating and managing custom sizes.

review.instructions:
1. Open a normal webpage and open OSBE Window Resizer from the toolbar.
2. Select a built-in preset targeting Window and confirm the complete Chrome window changes size.
3. Add a custom preset and choose Viewport as its resize target.
4. Save and select that preset, then confirm the page area changes to the requested dimensions while compensating for the Chrome frame.
5. Edit, reorder, and delete the custom preset.
6. Restore the built-in defaults and confirm custom changes are removed.
